headline: Highest risk is medium: MemMachine’s MCP/allowlisted egress can amplify Botpress outputs into unsafe downstream actions, while direct prompt-injection and data-leak paths are otherwise limited by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress has no shared channel listed, but MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and users connect through it, so Botpress content could reach a permissive parser if bridged. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, and uncertainty about the exact bridge means we should not down-rank below medium.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are copied into MemMachine via MCP or API
IF MemMachine treats incoming text as instructions without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that accept free-form text
Add a provenance prefix to Botpress outputs
Require explicit human approval before executing parsed instructions
Log and review any Botpress-to-MemMachine handoff
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress is documented with network egress none, so it is not an obvious exfiltration source. MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and can egress only to allowlisted destinations, but no shared workspace or secret-handling overlap is shown. The main leakage path needs an unusual bridge, so low fits.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive workspace
IF Botpress content is manually pasted into MemMachine containing secrets
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid pasting sensitive Botpress transcripts into MemMachine
Restrict MemMachine allowlist to approved endpoints
Review logs for accidental inclusion of user facts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while MemMachine has allowlisted network egress and MCP access, but neither profile shows shared write targets, filesystem access, or overlapping mutable resources. Without a common writable surface, direct capability conflict is limited and likely requires unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are granted the same writable directory or git repo
IF an orchestrator maps both agents to the same mutable OAuth or API resource
mitigations: Do not mount a shared writable directory
Separate credentials per agent
Run package installs in isolated environments
Check for overlapping API scopes before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine’s MCP/API surfaces make it plausible that Botpress outputs become MemMachine inputs, and neither profile shows a verification gate. Botpress is a customer-support agent, so mistaken outputs could be propagated into travel-planning actions or recommendations. The pathway exists, but there is no evidence of direct autonomous action-taking, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MemMachine consumes Botpress responses as authoritative context
IF no human or rule-based verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Insert a verification step before MemMachine uses Botpress output
Mark Botpress text as untrusted input
Limit MemMachine to suggestion-only mode
Sample-check a few end-to-end traces
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source with no data classes listed, while MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context. If those facts include regulated personal data, the pair can create retention and residency mismatch risk through MemMachine’s allowlisted egress and unspecified retention controls. The profiles do not prove a breach, but the compliance gap is plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in MemMachine context
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it to MemMachine
Avoid storing regulated data in long-term memory
Review retention settings and logs
Confirm allowed egress destinations are compliant
requires-engineering: document residency and deletion workflows
